title: Waterscapes for Promoting Mental Health in the General Population

findings.quote: Preliminary evidence has suggested that aquatic environments and riparian areas, i.e., waterscapes, can benefit psychological and mental wellbeing.

findings.consequent: Psychological and mental health compared to neighborhood green space
findings.quote: Additionally, the literature suggests that a neighborhood waterscape is more beneficial for psychological and mental health than a neighborhood green space [30,31].

findings.consequent: Psychological and mental health via mitigation (reduced urban heat island), instoration (physical activity, nature connectedness), and restoration (reduced anxiety/attentional fatigue)
findings.quote: Waterscapes are landscapes with an expanse of water which consist of water bodies and associated riparian habitats, including streams, rivers, lakes, wetlands, the coast, and their riparian zones, which can service psychological health benefits via the mechanisms of mitigation, instoration, and restoration [24,25].

findings.consequent: Psychological health (lowered pulse rate, muscle tone, increased skin temperature, reduced cardiovascular response to stress, alleviated anxiety)
findings.quote: It has been proved that bird and fish watching can not only lower pulse rate and muscle tone and increase skin temperature, but also bring about greater benefits for psychological health [48], which is related to the Biophilia Hypothesis [17].

findings.antecedent: Water features (sounds, color, clarity), especially low decibel water sounds
findings.consequent: Psychological and mental health (reduced noise, enhanced urban soundscape)
findings.quote: The water features of sounds, color and clarity are important sensory perceptions of waterscapes [65,85]. This can be due to people appreciating the sounds of water [69]... It has also been shown that noise reduction and enhancement of urban soundscapes are two important ways in which nature's sounds promote psychological and mental health [57,86].

findings.antecedent: Accessibility to waterscapes (e.g., <15 min walk, 300m distance)
findings.consequent: Psychological health (frequency of use, positive influence)
findings.quote: Accessibility, as a factor influencing people's frequency of using waterscapes, indirectly affects the contribution of waterscapes to psychological health [55].

findings.consequent: Human health and wellbeing (attention restoration, stress reduction, physical activity, psychological and emotional health)
findings.quote: Biodiversity within cities is critical to human health and wellbeing and provides a wide range of important ecosystem services [90-92].

findings.antecedent: Exercising in waterscapes (walking, exploring, talking, relaxing, swimming, sailing, surfing, rambling)
findings.quote: The waterside areas of urban blue spaces are particularly stimulating for dynamic activities, and it is indicated that living closer to waterscapes will be associated with higher levels of physical activity [54,74,96], such as walking, exploring, talking, and relaxing, which has the same positive impact on people's mental health as being active in urban green spaces [49].
